lines.trans: I implore you—at this rate my satellite channel will be finished.
Please, I beg you to lend me the money.
Mr. Muranishi's orders—he says to thin out the mosaic blur and sell them again.
Right now we just have to scrape together whatever cash we can.
I went and started the paperwork to sell off the villa and the cruiser.
The director won't be back all day raising funds. I'm sure he'll work something out.
Calling it tax planning, he kept thirty million yen of my pay on deposit.
Isn't that guy way too irresponsible? His priorities are completely backward.
This is fraud! He secretly embezzled the wages we earned with our own bodies.
That's going too far. Complaining behind his back right now won't help anything.
You're so blindly devoted to the director it creeps me out!
He's our director! Believing in him is only natural!

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Humble (kenjougo) equivalent of する, used in polite business and apologetic expressions.

examples.text: すぐにご連絡いたします。
examples.trans: I will contact you right away.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: More formal counterpart of じゃあ used in business and polite conversation.

examples.text: 衛星チャンネルの放送権を一つわたくしに許可してください。
examples.trans: Please grant me the broadcast rights to one satellite channel.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: 会議は何時に終わりますか。
examples.trans: What time does the meeting end?

meanings.note: Auxiliary godan verb following て-form.

examples.text: つい忘れてしまいました。
本を全部読んでしまった。
examples.trans: I finished reading the whole book.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Polite/standard form of 金 (かね) with honorific prefix お.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 村西さんの指示。もう一回モザイクを薄くして売るんだって。
examples.trans: Mr. Muranishi's orders—he says to thin out the mosaic blur and sell them again.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Read いちにち for duration/rate ('per day'); read ついたち for the 1st of the month.

examples.text: 一日十五分勉強します。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: go home; leave and go back
meanings.note: Repeated past form 帰った、帰った! is an idiomatic shooing command ('off you go, go on home!').

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
